title: Thinking Machines puts a strong open model on your laptop. A test with two million booby-trapped prompts finds AI providers leaking data, and Signal blocks phone AI from reading chats. ChatGPT Space reaches Plus, OpenAI’s new usage rules take effect, and Trump threatens a tax on data centres abroad.
summary: Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is an open model with 26.4 billion parameters that runs in about 20GB on a 32GB Mac and leads open models under 100 billion parameters on the DeepSWE coding test, by the lab’s figures. Dragos seeded about two million prompts with trackable secrets and found breached providers, resellers keeping prompts and ignored privacy settings; OpenRouter has dropped three providers and pulled 125 endpoints from its Zero Data Retention list. Signal now blocks screenshots and on-screen AI by default on iOS 27 and when Android assistants try to read it. ChatGPT Space, with shared pages and slides that update from connected tools, is rolling out to Plus. OpenAI’s usage policies now require approval for model resellers and bar using outputs to train rival models. Trump said US firms building data centres abroad would face a “tremendous tax”.
uncertainty: Inkling 2 Mini’s benchmark scores are Thinking Machines’ own. The Dragos findings are one firm’s research; not all affected providers have posted, and OpenRouter’s actions are as it describes them. Signal’s blocking depends on app and system versions and does not cover macOS. Space is rolling out to eligible Plus accounts gradually. Trump’s tax remark came with no details, legal text or date.

stories.theme: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open model small enough to run on a 32GB laptop and strong at coding
stories.changed: On 20 November 2026 Thinking Machines Lab, the company led by Mira Murati, released Inkling 2 Mini with open weights under the Apache 2.0 licence. It has 26.4 billion parameters, of which 3.4 billion are used for each word it writes, and it runs the middle 12 of its 24 layers three times per word, a design called looping that lets it reason more without being bigger. The download is about 20GB, and the model card lists Apple silicon Macs with 32GB or more of memory, Nvidia’s DGX Spark, or graphics cards with 32GB or more as suitable. It reads text and images and handles up to a million tokens of context. The lab says it leads every open-weights model under 100 billion parameters on coding tests such as DeepSWE v1.1, at 48.2%. It is on Hugging Face, runs through Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp and others, and is on the lab’s Tinker service for fine-tuning. The model card warns that, when using tools, it “may take destructive actions, such as deleting or overwriting files, without confirmation” and tells developers to run agent work in a sandbox.
stories.matters: A capable coding and agent model that runs offline on a well-specced laptop means some AI work no longer has to leave your machine. That helps with privacy, cost and working without a connection.
stories.imply: Local does not mean safe to leave alone. The lab itself says the model is less reliable than bigger ones at following instructions and may not report its results accurately. It also knows fewer facts than larger models, so pair it with search or your own documents.
uses: Run it on a 32GB Mac to summarise or tag files that should not go to a cloud service.
Try it as an offline coding helper on a flight or a train, inside a sandboxed folder.
Fine-tune it on Tinker for one narrow, repeated task, such as sorting support tickets.
stories.example: A consultant installs it with Ollama on a 48GB MacBook, points it at a folder of client notes copied into a sandbox, and asks for a one-page summary per client without anything leaving the laptop.
stories.audience: Developers, privacy-minded teams and anyone with a recent high-memory Mac or AI desktop.
stories.watch: Independent benchmark checks, how it behaves on real agent work at home, and whether other labs answer with small looped models.

source.title: Thinking Machines Lab: Introducing Inkling 2 Mini, 20 November 2026
source.quote: Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

stories.theme: A test with two million booby-trapped prompts found AI providers leaking data; OpenRouter dropped three providers
stories.changed: On 19 November 2026 HD Moore, chief research officer at the security firm Dragos, published the results of a five-month test. From July to November his team sent about two million prompts containing unique, trackable secrets, such as fake cloud keys and private web links, to widely used AI services, then watched where those secrets turned up. He reports evidence that at least three AI providers were breached by attackers who copied incoming prompts, that some resellers in an inference marketplace logged and kept customer prompts, and that several providers ignored “Zero Data Retention” and “no data collection” settings. In one case, prompts sent to US hosts of a Chinese lab’s models were fetched by that lab’s systems days later. On 22 November OpenRouter, a popular AI router that passes requests on to many model providers, said it had off-boarded three providers, removed 125 endpoints from its Zero Data Retention list and notified potentially affected customers. It said the findings showed no breach of OpenRouter itself.
stories.matters: Many AI apps send your text through a router and on to whichever provider is cheapest. Each hop can read it. A privacy setting is only a promise, and this test shows some providers did not keep it.
stories.imply: The cheapest model route can be the leakiest. Dragos advises going direct to a first-tier provider where you can, picking upstream providers yourself rather than accepting a router’s default pool, and staying away from reseller marketplaces. Keep passwords and keys out of prompts either way.
uses: Ask your AI vendors which providers actually handle your prompts, and get it in writing.
Turn off automatic provider pools in routers and allow only providers you have checked.
Plant a fake credential, such as a free Canarytoken, in your own agent prompts and treat any use as an incident.
stories.example: A startup that routes customer chats through OpenRouter restricts traffic to two first-tier providers, adds a canary key to its system prompt, and sets an alert if anyone ever tries to use it.
stories.audience: Developers and IT or security teams using AI routers, gateways or cheap inference resellers.
stories.watch: Write-ups from the affected providers, whether other routers such as Vercel publish their own checks, and whether ZDR labels come with proof.

source.title: OpenRouter: Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers, 22 November 2026
source.quote: Off-boarded three providers from OpenRouter, based on the results of our investigations.

stories.theme: Signal now blocks screenshots by default so phone AI assistants cannot read your chats
stories.changed: On 20 November 2026 Signal said it is blocking AI agents built into phone operating systems from capturing what is on screen in its app. Signal president Meredith Whittaker wrote that features such as Gemini on Android and Siri AI’s on-screen awareness on iOS 27 scan the screen, so Signal messages can end up stored wherever the operating system’s AI keeps its data, outside Signal’s control. On iPhone, with Signal 8.37 or later on iOS 27, the new Block Siri AI setting is on by default and stops screenshots, screen recordings and on-device AI from reading Signal. On Android, with Signal 8.35.1 or later, screen security switches on the first time an AI assistant tries to read the screen. Users can turn it off, or on iPhone switch it off for 10 minutes to take a screenshot. Whittaker called the fix incomplete: it does not stop AI agents reaching data in other ways, such as through files on the device, and Signal cannot do the same on macOS yet.
stories.matters: Phone makers are building AI that reads everything on your screen. Signal is the first big app to push back by default, and its warning applies to any app where you read sensitive work messages.
stories.imply: Encryption protects messages in transit, but not once an on-screen assistant has read them. Companies that allow phone AI assistants on work devices should decide which apps those assistants may see.
uses: Update Signal and check the new setting under Settings, Privacy.
For work phones, review whether Gemini or Siri AI may read the screen in email, chat and banking apps.
Tell colleagues that screenshots in Signal will now be blocked by default, so they are not surprised.
stories.example: An HR lead who discusses staff cases on Signal updates the app, leaves Block Siri AI on, and asks IT whether the company’s other messaging apps offer a similar setting.
stories.audience: Anyone who handles confidential conversations on a phone, and IT teams managing mobile devices.
stories.watch: Whether Apple, Google and Microsoft give apps proper ways to block AI reading, and whether other messaging apps follow Signal.

source.title: Signal: Signal is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy, 20 November 2026
source.quote: So, we are blocking such capture by preventing screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android.

stories.theme: ChatGPT Space, for shared pages and slides that ChatGPT keeps up to date, is rolling out to Plus
stories.changed: On 20 November 2026 OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT Space to Plus users aged 18 and older worldwide. Until now it was limited to Pro, Business and Enterprise. Space is a home for pages, slides, images and uploaded files, and replaces the old Library. You can ask ChatGPT to create an editable page or presentation, invite others with Space access to edit it with you in real time, and set pages and slides to update themselves from connected apps and tools. OpenAI’s examples include a to-do list that updates itself and a project plan that stays current with decisions from Slack. Pages can now be edited on iOS and Android. People on the free plan cannot open shared pages, and there are no public links. OpenAI’s help page says each collaborator’s own Memory and training settings apply when their ChatGPT reads a shared page, so your contributions may be used for training through a collaborator whose setting is on.
stories.matters: The Plus plan now gets shared, self-updating documents inside ChatGPT. That puts it closer to Notion or Google Docs for small teams and freelancers.
stories.imply: Sharing has privacy catches. Anything ChatGPT copies onto a page is visible to everyone who can view it, even if they cannot open the original source, and one collaborator’s training setting can expose your edits.
uses: Turn a meeting chat into a shared page with decisions and next steps.
Keep a client status page that updates from your connected tools.
Build a short slide deck with a colleague, each using your own ChatGPT.
stories.example: Two freelancers on Plus build a shared project plan page, connect it to their Slack, and check it each Monday instead of writing a status email.
stories.audience: Plus subscribers, freelancers and small teams that already plan work in ChatGPT.
stories.watch: When Space reaches your account, when Sheets arrive, and how Business admins control sharing.

source.title: OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT release notes, 20 November 2026
source.quote: Starting today, ChatGPT Space is rolling out globally to Plus users ages 18 and older.

stories.theme: OpenAI’s new usage rules are now in force: model resellers need approval, and outputs cannot train rival models
stories.changed: OpenAI’s rewritten Usage Policies took effect on 20 November 2026, a month after it announced them on 21 October. The full text is now public. Any company that runs a “model-access intermediary” platform, such as an AI router or gateway that lets other people or companies use OpenAI models directly, now needs OpenAI’s prior review and approval. The policy says this does not apply just because an app uses OpenAI models to power its own features. A new section bars using OpenAI models or their outputs to create or prepare training data, training tasks, rubrics or feedback for models meant as alternatives to or substitutes for OpenAI’s. The rewrite also covers protections for children and teens, requirements for high-stakes uses, and approval for national security and law enforcement uses.
stories.matters: If your company resells or routes OpenAI access to others, you now need permission. If you only build features on top of OpenAI, you do not. The full text now draws a line that was unclear in October.
stories.imply: Teams that use GPT output to label or score data for other models, including open models they plan to swap in, should check whether that work now breaks the rules.
uses: Ask legal whether any internal gateway lets outside parties use OpenAI models directly.
Check data pipelines that use GPT to create training or evaluation data for other models.
Ask AI vendors whether they are a reseller or a feature builder under the new policy.
stories.example: A product team that uses GPT-6.2 to grade answers for training a cheaper in-house model pauses that job and asks legal to check it against the new training section.
stories.audience: Developers, AI platform teams, legal and procurement teams that buy or resell AI access.
stories.watch: How strictly OpenAI enforces the intermediary rule, and whether Anthropic and Google publish similar terms.

source.title: OpenAI: Usage policies (effective 20 November 2026)
source.quote: If you operate a model-access intermediary platform or other service that enables third parties to directly access OpenAI models, you must obtain our prior review and approval.

stories.theme: Trump says US companies that build data centres abroad will face a “tremendous tax”
stories.changed: At a White House press conference on 20 November 2026, President Donald Trump said US companies would not be allowed to build data centres outside the country, and that those who did would face what he called a “tremendous tax”. CNBC reports that he said the policy was news to his own staff: “I haven’t even said that to my people.” No details, legal basis or start date were given. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle already run data centres abroad, often to sit close to customers or to meet local data rules. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not immediately comment, CNBC said. Reuters notes the remark came days after the Commerce Department restricted exports of advanced AI chips to several Southeast Asian countries.
stories.matters: Where cloud companies build decides where your data can be stored and how fast AI services respond in India, Europe and elsewhere. A tax on foreign builds could raise prices or slow new regions.
stories.imply: This is a spoken threat, not a law. Nothing changes for cloud customers today, but long-term contracts that depend on a new local region are worth checking.
uses: List which of your AI and cloud services rely on data centres outside the US.
Ask your cloud account manager whether announced local regions are on schedule.
Keep data-residency requirements written into contracts rather than assumed.
stories.example: A bank in India planning to move AI workloads to a new local cloud region asks its provider for written confirmation of the region’s launch date and data-residency terms.
stories.audience: IT leaders, cloud buyers and anyone with data-residency obligations outside the US.
stories.watch: Any executive order or bill with details, responses from the cloud companies, and reactions from countries hosting US data centres.

source.title: CNBC: Trump vows to stop U.S. companies from building data centers abroad, threatens ‘tremendous tax’, 20 November 2026
source.quote: they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them.

signals.raw: Thinking Machines, 20 Nov: Inkling 2 Mini, open weights, Apache 2.0; 26.4B params, 3.4B active, 5.4B weight activations per token with three loops; ~20GB; Macs with 32GB+; 1M ctx; DeepSWE v1.1 48.2%, Vals Index v2.2 46.5% (lab figures); model card: may take destructive actions, run agents in a sandbox.

Dragos (HD Moore), 19 Nov: ~2M prompts with canaries, July to November; at least three providers compromised; marketplace resellers logged prompts; ZDR and no-data-collection flags ignored. OpenRouter, 22 Nov: off-boarded three providers, removed 125 endpoints from ZDR, notified customers.

Signal blog (Meredith Whittaker), 20 Nov: blocking screenshots on iOS 27 and when Android AI assistants try to read the screen; Block Siri AI on by default on iPhone (Signal 8.37+); Android 8.35.1+; not on macOS; remedy incomplete.

OpenAI release notes, 20 Nov: ChatGPT Space rolling out globally to Plus users 18+; shared pages and slides; auto-update from connected apps; replaces Library; mobile editing; Free cannot open shared pages; no public links.

OpenAI Usage Policies, effective 20 Nov: model-access intermediaries need prior review and approval, not apps that merely integrate models; no using models or outputs to prepare training material for substitute models; changelog dated 21 Oct.
CNBC, 20 Nov: Trump says US companies will face a ‘tremendous tax’ for building data centers abroad; said he had not told his staff; Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Oracle did not immediately comment.
